blocks.content: Quiz: Why does pagedEntries have filteredEntries in its dependency array?
Tap an option below to answer:
To ensure the page number resets to 1 when the search changes
The page reset happens in handleQueryChange(). The dependency array only controls when useMemo() recomputes.
The page reset happens in handleQueryChange(). The dependency array only controls when useMemo() recomputes.
Because pagedEntries is a slice of filteredEntries; if the filter result changes, the page slice must recompute
pagedEntries is derived from filteredEntries, so it must be a dependency.
pagedEntries is derived from filteredEntries, so it must be a dependency.
Because useMemo() always requires the previous useMemo() result as a dependency
useMemo() dependencies are whatever values the function actually uses, not an automatic chain.
useMemo() dependencies are whatever values the function actually uses, not an automatic chain.
To prevent stale entries from appearing on the current page
Preventing staleness is a side effect of listing the right dependencies, not the reason filteredEntries is listed.
Preventing staleness is a side effect of listing the right dependencies, not the reason filteredEntries is listed.
